title: 말의 높낮이 한눈에: 누구에게 어떻게 말해요?
objective: You can choose the right speech level for a listener or text and change a sentence between the four levels.
summary: This sheet compares Korean's four main speech levels in one table so you can pick the right ending.

task.title: Choose and change endings
task.line: Look at who is listening or what is being written, then choose or write the ending that fits.

forms.when: News, announcements, presentations, meetings, customer service, speaking to a group.
forms.means: The most formal and polite level. Use -습니다 after a consonant (먹습니다) and -ㅂ니다 after a vowel (갑니다). Verb stems ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ and take -ㅂ니다 (만들다 → 만듭니다).
forms.exampleMeaning: The next station is Seoul Station.

forms.form: 해요체 (informal polite) — Statement / Question / Command: -아요/-어요/-해요 | Noun: 이에요/예요
forms.when: Everyday talk with people you don't know well, older people, coworkers, shop staff.
forms.means: Polite but soft. The same ending works for statements, questions and requests.
forms.exampleMeaning: I commute to work by subway every day.

forms.form: 해체 (반말, casual) — Statement / Question / Command: -아/-어/-해 | Noun: 야/이야
forms.when: Close friends, younger siblings, people of the same age who agreed to speak casually.
forms.means: This is 해요체 without 요, except after nouns: 이에요/예요 become 이야/야 (우산이에요 → 우산이야), and 아니에요 becomes 아니야. Use 나/내 instead of 저/제.
forms.exampleMeaning: Where are you now? I'm at the library.

forms.form: 해라체 (plain) — Statement: verb -ㄴ다/-는다, adjective -다, noun -(이)다 | Question: -니?/-냐? | Command: -아라/-어라 | Suggestion: -자
forms.when: Writing: diaries, newspapers, reports, essays. In speech: parents to children, or to much younger people.
forms.means: A neutral, plain style. Verbs take -ㄴ다 after a vowel (간다) and -는다 after a consonant (읽는다). Verb stems ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ and take -ㄴ다 (만들다 → 만든다).
forms.example: 오늘은 비가 온다. 나는 집에서 책을 읽는다.
forms.exampleMeaning: It is raining today. I am reading a book at home.

watchOut: 나는 매일 아침 빵을 먹다 (X) → 먹는다 (O): The dictionary form is not a sentence. In 해라체, verbs need -ㄴ다/-는다.
날씨가 좋는다 (X) → 좋다 (O): Adjectives take only -다, not -는다.
우리 언니이야 (X) → 우리 언니야 (O): Use 야 after a vowel and 이야 after a consonant (동생이야).
선생님, 어디 가? (X) → 선생님, 어디 가요? (O): Don't use 해체 with teachers, bosses or strangers.
exercises: Choose the right ending for each situation: ① News (뉴스): 내일은 전국에 눈이 (와 / 옵니다). ② To a close friend (친한 친구에게): 주말에 뭐 (합니까 / 해)? ③ Diary (일기): 오늘은 정말 (피곤했어요 / 피곤했다).
Change each sentence to 합쇼체 for a meeting: ① 저는 매주 수영장에 가요. ② 이 식당은 김치찌개가 맛있어요. ③ 회의는 몇 시에 시작해요?
You are talking to a close friend. Rewrite each sentence in 해체: ① 저는 오늘 바빠요. ② 이건 제 우산이에요.
Each sentence has the wrong ending. Write the correct one: ① A student to a teacher (학생이 선생님께): 선생님, 숙제 다 했어. ② Newspaper article (신문 기사): 요즘 물가가 계속 오르는다.
A parent is talking to a child. Write the 해라체 form of the word in ( ): ① 밥 빨리 ____. (먹다, command) ② 숙제 다 ____? (하다, past, question) ③ 우리 같이 공원에 ____. (가다, suggestion)
answers: ① 옵니다 ② 해 ③ 피곤했다
① 저는 매주 수영장에 갑니다. ② 이 식당은 김치찌개가 맛있습니다. ③ 회의는 몇 시에 시작합니까?
① 나는 오늘 바빠. (난 오늘 바빠.) ② 이건 내 우산이야.
① 먹어라 ② 했니? (했냐?) ③ 가자
